landing.heroDescription: Hold a credential from a trusted issuer, generate an UltraHonk zero-knowledge proof locally, and verify your claim on Stellar — without the underlying data ever touching the chain.
landing.step1Body: A trusted issuer signs a credential to your wallet. It lives on your device — never on a server.
landing.step2Body: Generate a zero-knowledge proof locally in your browser. Only the claim leaves; the data behind it never does.
landing.step3Body: Any Stellar protocol reads ProofRegistry on-chain. One proof, valid across every protocol, for 30 days.
landing.verifiedOnceDescription: Any protocol on Stellar can verify your credentials in one contract call. No API. No backend. No re-verification.
landing.verifyDirectlyBody: Visit StellarCred before using any app. Your credentials work everywhere, instantly.
landing.verifyThroughAppBody: Apps that integrate StellarCred show a "Verify" button. Complete verification and return automatically.
landing.userReturnsVerifiedBody: On-chain proof, read in one call. No backend needed.
landing.readyToTryBody: Connect a Stellar wallet on testnet, get a credential, generate your first on-chain ZK proof in under a minute.

developers.title: Integrate StellarCred
developers.howItWorksBody: StellarCred stores zero-knowledge proofs on Stellar. Your protocol reads them with one contract call. No API keys, no backend, no data handling — the only thing you trust is the on-chain
developers.checkingAClaimBody: The primary call. Returns true if the wallet has a valid, unexpired proof of the claim. For parameterised claims (age, income, funds), pass minThreshold to enforce the threshold on-chain — trustlessly.
developers.fetchingAllClaimsBody: Protocols that gate on multiple claims simultaneously benefit from fetching everything at once rather than making N separate hasClaim calls.
developers.configurationBody: Call configure() once at startup, or set env vars. Both approaches work in Node.js, Next.js, and edge runtimes.
developers.missingRegistryNote: A missing registryId doesn't throw — it makes every hasClaim/getClaims call silently return false/[], which can look like "nobody is verified" instead of "misconfigured." Use healthCheck() to diagnose it directly (a dev-only console warning also fires automatically the first time this happens).
developers.redirectingUsersBody: If a user hasn't verified yet, send them to StellarCred and get them back automatically. Use claimParams to customise thresholds.
developers.returnUrlNote: The return URL params are untrusted hints, not a proof. Nothing binds this redirect to your session — anyone can craft a URL shaped exactly like a real one and open it. Use parseReturnParams to read them, but always re-verify with hasClaim against the on-chain ProofRegistry (ideally server-side) before granting access.
developers.callingContractDirectlyBody: Prefer Soroban? Call ProofRegistry from your own contract — no SDK required. Use is_verified for binary claims and check_claim for threshold enforcement. Both take a trailing trusted_issuers parameter — pass None to accept a proof from any registered issuer (unchanged default), or Some(vec![...]) to restrict a claim to specific issuers, e.g. accepting KYC only from Persona or Jumio.

docs.aboutDescription: Zero-knowledge credential infrastructure on Stellar. Prove facts about yourself without the data ever touching the chain.
docs.overviewBody1: StellarCred is a zero-knowledge credential system built on Stellar. It lets a trusted issuer sign claims about a holder — KYC status, age, income, jurisdiction — and lets that holder later prove those claims on-chain without revealing the underlying data.
docs.overviewBody2: Every proof is generated locally in the holder's browser using the UltraHonk proof system (Noir 1.0.0-beta.9 / Barretenberg 0.87.0). The Stellar chain stores only a compact verification record — no personal data touches the ledger.
docs.coreGuaranteeBody: A verifier reading ProofRegistry.is_verified learns that a holder satisfies a claim, and nothing else. Not their name, date of birth, income figure, or country — only the boolean result.
docs.credentialTypesBody: Each credential type has a dedicated Noir circuit. The circuit proves the claim using the commitment, the issuer's signature, and optional public parameters — all without revealing the underlying attribute.
docs.ultrahonkBody: StellarCred uses the UltraHonk proving system from the Aztec Barretenberg library. UltraHonk is a PLONK-family argument over the BN254 elliptic curve with a Keccak transcript, matching the on-chain verifier exposed as a Soroban host function in Stellar Protocol 22.
docs.poseidon2Body: The credential stores a Poseidon2 hash of the attribute value and a random 248-bit salt:
docs.poseidon2Note: Poseidon2 is ZK-friendly — it is cheap to prove inside a Noir circuit while being collision-resistant. The salt prevents dictionary attacks on the commitment even for low-entropy values like country codes.
docs.secp256k1Body: After computing the commitment, the issuer signs it with a secp256k1 ECDSA key using prehash: false — Noir uses the raw 32-byte commitment as the message digest directly. Each Noir circuit verifies this signature inside the proof, binding the claim to a specific registered issuer public key.
docs.demoKeyNote: The demo issuer's signing key lives only in the Next.js server process — never in the browser. In production, each issuer would hold their own secret key in a hardware security module or secrets manager.
docs.smartContractsBody: Four Soroban contracts are deployed on Stellar testnet. They are wired at deploy time and communicate through typed contract clients (no shared library dependencies between them).
docs.publicInputBody: Each circuit outputs the following public inputs (32 bytes per field, big-endian):
docs.commitmentNote: The commitment that appears in the public inputs is a hash — it reveals nothing about the underlying value without the salt. Even if the chain is public, an observer learns only that some holder with some credential passed verification at a given time.
docs.storageBody: Your credentials — including the raw attribute value (date of birth, income, balance…) and its random salt — are stored only in this browser's localStorage, under the key stellarcred:credentials. There is no StellarCred account and no server-side credential database: the credential JSON exists only on the device that received it.
docs.credentialsAreBrowserSpecific: Credentials are browser-specific and can be lost permanently.
docs.credentialsAreBrowserSpecificBody: Clearing site data, switching to a different browser or device, or browsing in private/incognito mode erases them — there is no server-side copy to recover them from. Back up (below) before any of those happen.
docs.backupBody1: Open the Holder page and click Export backup — the browser downloads a JSON file containing every credential. Keep that file somewhere safe: it contains the raw sensitive attribute values, so treat it like a password.
docs.backupBody2: To restore — on a new browser, a new device, or after clearing site data — open the Holder page there, click Import credential JSON, and paste the file's contents. Restored credentials generate and submit proofs exactly like newly issued ones.
docs.transferToDeviceBody: To move a single credential to another device, open its details (click the credential on the Holder page) and choose Transfer to another device. You pick a passphrase and the app shows a QR code; the credential is encrypted with that passphrase (AES-256-GCM, key derived via PBKDF2) before it ever becomes a QR code, so the code alone reveals nothing. On the other device, scan the QR and enter the same passphrase to import.
docs.getStartedBody: The fastest way to see StellarCred in action on testnet — no local build needed:
docs.step1: Install a Stellar wallet (Freighter, Albedo, xBull, and others are supported) and switch it to Testnet
docs.step2: Fund your address via Stellar Friendbot
docs.step3: Click Verify in the nav, connect your wallet, and request a KYC credential
docs.step4: Go to Wallet, click Generate proof — the browser proves in ~10 seconds
docs.step5: Click Submit to Stellar, approve in your wallet, and check the Apps page to see your eligibility update live
